name: Priya Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m from the independent Work Futures Panel. Your answers stay confidential. What does a normal day at your accounting firm look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, with a bachelor’s degree in accounting, but I am still a junior preparing accounts and tax returns and I know I have more to learn. I like finding the receipt that makes a client’s figures honest; I dislike being hurried past a question I cannot yet answer. Noel and I have grown children living on their own, lower wages, and only about two weeks of bills saved, so retirement is in sight but not settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the machines only do a little, I can still see the tax folder on my desk. I would rather check a real receipt than guess what the software meant.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a person must call the client before changing a figure on a return. A wrong number is still our responsibility.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used an AI tool, and I know I take longer than the other juniors on a new return. My partner Noel drives delivery rounds, but our lower wages and barely two weeks saved already make me nervous about rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the accounts assigned to me and use my paper tick list before I pass a return to the senior reviewer. I would cancel the paid meal box at the next renewal and put the freed fifteen a month into an emergency tin if groceries still fit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our money as it is, even with work staying much the same. One repair to my partner Noel’s van could use the whole little cushion.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did your paper check help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Thursday a client had two nearly identical fuel receipts, and my tick list made me call before I counted both. The senior reviewer, Miriam, checked my correction before we filed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will cancelling the box actually save money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The meal box renews on the first Monday of the month. We can buy ordinary groceries instead, but if they cost more, I will not pretend the tin has gained fifteen.

say: I would **call clients** before changing a doubtful tax figure.
I would keep my **paper tick list** beside each assigned return.
think: My junior work is slow to learn, and I have **never used AI**.
Two weeks of **savings** leave our rent exposed even in a mild change.
do: Keep preparing **assigned accounts** with the paper tick list and Miriam’s review.
Cancel the **meal box** at renewal; save fifteen monthly only if replacement groceries cost less.
feel: **Anxious** about existing low wages and van repair risk.
S0.quote: One repair to my partner Noel’s van could use the whole little cushion.
fieldNote: Priya’s **paper tick list** caught duplicated fuel receipts, fitting her careful but slower junior work and reluctance to use AI.
The **meal box** produces new emergency cash only if ordinary groceries genuinely cost less than the cancelled subscription.

steps.text: Keep assigned accounts with paper tick list and Miriam’s review
Cancel paid meal box at next renewal
Save fifteen monthly only if replacement groceries cost less

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing and checking returns are my whole shift, so this change would be felt here, not years later when robots appear. I would ask Miriam what work a junior is still paid to do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients to ring the office if an automated figure looks wrong. Someone should answer the telephone and know their file.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid hours will be cut when the firm checks routine returns by machine. With two weeks saved and few accounting jobs nearby, I cannot wait quietly for a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Miriam for paid supervised time to learn how the client calls and correction letters are handled; if she gives me two assigned calls, I will do them with her beside me. If she refuses, I will practise on free sample letters at home while keeping only paid tax files still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because a cut in my own week would hit rent immediately. I will learn a new part of the office if they actually pay me to work at it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your paid day disappears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a paid day goes, I will apply for posted billing clerk jobs at the local hospital. I would accept only written wages that cover our rent and food, with a confirmed start and hours that fit Noel’s van schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the supervised calls involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have handled corrections on paper, but not a whole client call alone. Miriam would need to assign the call and paid time, and check what I say before it goes into the record.

say: I would ask what **junior work** remains paid when routine checks move to software.
I would ask clients to **ring the office** about a doubtful automated figure.
think: I expect **my own hours** to be cut in this change.
Two weeks saved and **few nearby firms** leave little room to wait.
do: Learn **two supervised client calls** only if Miriam assigns paid time; otherwise practise free letters while paid files last.
Seek **posted hospital billing** after cuts with written rent-and-food pay, confirmed start and hours fitting Noel’s schedule.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing rent money through shorter hours.
S1.quote: I expect my paid hours will be cut when the firm checks routine returns by machine.
fieldNote: Her **client-call learning** is a real paid assignment with Miriam supervising, not an enquiry that assumes training will appear.
If refused, **free letters** and current paid files are the fallback; a hospital move needs an advertised written offer.

steps.text: Handle two client calls only if Miriam assigns supervised paid time
Otherwise practise free letters while paid tax files remain offered
Seek posted hospital billing after cuts with written rent-and-food pay, confirmed start and Noel-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could write and check our accounts before the hands-on robots arrive around 2031. My desk does not get those three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the office that every junior needs a date for their last paid shift if the firm cuts the work. I would not accept a rumour in place of a letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my tax hours to end in the first year after 2028, and Noel’s delivery wage alone cannot pay the rent. If my tax wage ends in 2028, our two weeks of savings would be gone almost at once.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stop the meal box now and ask our grown daughter Ruth whether we could stay in her spare room for one month if both my salary ends and the rent cannot be met. After job loss, I will apply for posted hospital billing shifts only if written pay covers rent and food and a start date is fixed; until then I will take paid firm closeout files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed and ashamed that I may need to ask Ruth for a room. She has her own life, so I will ask rather than assume she can take us in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you ask your daughter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ruth lives across town and has a spare room, but I have not asked her yet. I would say it is one month and we would contribute groceries if she agrees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the hospital job be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Noel can keep driving while I look for a posted paid shift. A hospital job is still desk billing, so I cannot promise it survives AGI; I only know it is one of the few actual employers nearby.

say: I would ask for **written last-shift dates** if junior tax work ends.
I would not promise **hospital billing** is safe from AGI.
think: I expect my **tax hours** to end after 2028.
Two weeks saved and Noel’s wage cannot cover the **rent gap**.
do: Stop the **meal box** now and ask Ruth about a one-month room only if salary ends and rent fails.
Seek **posted hospital billing** after loss with written rent-and-food pay and fixed start; retain only offered paid closeout files.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected income loss and the possibility of asking family.
S2.quote: If my tax wage ends in 2028, our two weeks of savings would be gone almost at once.
fieldNote: Her **family request** is conditional on a real rent gap and Ruth’s agreement, not an assumed housing transfer.
She recognises **hospital desk exposure** too; posted wages and dates matter more than calling another office safe.

steps.text: Stop paid meal box now to reduce bills
Ask Ruth about one month only if salary ends and rent fails
Seek posted billing work after loss with written rent-and-food pay and fixed start
Take paid firm closeout files only while offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 gives us time to find a paid place to learn another office task. It does not change that the tax desk meets AGI before 2034 robots are useful.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to put junior training places and pay in writing. I would rather be shown a real billing file than handed a promise of future work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may lose this junior wage after 2031, even with more time to prepare. Noel and I cannot call retirement a solution when we have only two weeks saved and no known income to replace my pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would apply for a posted paid hospital billing trainee place and accept supervised practice only if the hospital covers any fees, pays the training hours, and gives written wages, start date and shifts that cover rent and fit Noel’s schedule. If there is no suitable place, I will work through free public billing examples while keeping assigned paid returns only while the firm offers them, including the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because I can seek a real placement over five years, but the household still needs wages. I do not want to spend our food money on a course advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the placement teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A billing trainee should learn to match a patient statement to an invoice and ask before changing a charge. I would practise that with a supervisor on an assigned file, not on someone’s private record at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no suitable hospital role appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will check the hospital postings each month. If no vacancy opens or the wages do not cover rent, I keep current paid firm work while it exists and continue the free examples.

say: I would demand **written paid trainee places**, not a future-work promise.
I would set **2031** as the tax desk deadline, before later robots.
think: Retirement is no answer without **known replacement income**.
Two weeks saved means a **paid placement** must be real.
do: Learn **hospital billing** only in a posted paid place with funded fees, paid supervision, written rent-covering wage/start and Noel-compatible shifts.
If no suitable place opens, study **free billing examples** while assigned paid tax work remains.
feel: **Anxious** about later wage loss, with time to seek a placement.
S3.quote: I would rather be shown a real billing file than handed a promise of future work.
fieldNote: The **billing practice** involves a real assigned statement, a supervisor, funded fees and paid hours in a posted place.
Her **free-example fallback** and current tax files remain available only while the firm continues paying for work.

steps.text: Take posted billing practice only with funded fees, paid supervision, written rent-covering wage/start and Noel-compatible shifts
Study free billing examples while assigned paid returns remain offered after 2031
Check hospital trainee postings monthly; accept only written rent-covering pay, start and Noel-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 puts me at 68. Birthdays do not pay rent. Full AGI would still reach the office in 2036 before robots arrived around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to keep careful client records while we are still paid for them. I would ask Miriam to say each year whether the junior shifts are likely to stay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to stop working someday, but I have no settled income figure that lets me choose a date. Our grown children have their own bills, and I will not assume they can carry ours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep taking assigned paid returns and, if groceries and rent permit, put eight from my wages into the emergency tin each month. If junior shifts are cut after 2036, I will seek posted hospital records work only with written wages covering rent and food, confirmed start and workable hours; I will stay with any firm work actually paid until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because the long runway still depends on earnings. If the paid shifts end, the two-week reserve would make it frightening quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would that small saving work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Eight is a small transfer, but it is new money from the wage, not money already in the tin. I would stop it if Noel’s van needs a repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your daughter for help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not ask Ruth to fund our retirement. I would ask her for a temporary room only if the rent truly failed and she said she could manage it.

say: I would ask Miriam for **annual junior-shift dates** while we still have paid work.
I would keep **client records** sound while preparing them.
think: I cannot set a **retirement date** without known replacement income.
Our grown children have **their own bills**; we cannot assume their support.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** while offered and save eight monthly from wages only if rent and groceries permit.
Seek **posted hospital records** after 2036 cuts with written rent-and-food pay, confirmed start and workable hours; retain only offered firm work.
Ask my **daughter Ruth** for a temporary room only if rent fails and she agrees.
feel: **Anxious** about earnings despite the long runway.
fieldNote: At **68 in 2036**, Priya will not assume a pension or turn grown children into a planned income source.
Her **eight monthly** is new wage cash and stops for essential costs; outside work still needs posted written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns only while firm offers them
Save eight monthly from wages if rent and groceries allow; stop for van repair
Seek posted hospital records after 2036 cuts with written rent-and-food pay, confirmed start and workable hours
Ask daughter for temporary room only if rent fails and she agrees

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my junior tax shifts to end before we can replace the rent money. A real posted billing job with written wages and start, or a paid supervised place to learn, would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I would stop caring about the clients if I lost the desk. I would remember the client who brought me two fuel receipts long after the firm stopped paying me to check them.

headlineQuote: I would remember the client who brought me two fuel receipts long after the firm stopped paying me to check them.
portrait: Priya is a **58 year old junior** accountant with a bachelor’s degree who learns tax work through paper checks and senior review.
She has **never used AI** and prefers familiar records, client calls and supervised practice over untested software.
Noel’s delivery wage, grown children, **two weeks saved**, lower pay and few nearby accounting firms make the plateau anxious.
She seeks **posted paid billing work** with supervised learning and written household fitting terms, keeping family help conditional.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could end her paid junior tax shifts before rent money is replaced.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted billing job** with written wages and start, or a paid supervised place to learn, would help.
